title: Frequently Asked Questions
description: Answers about Peer Support Groups and how Badger Supports works.

items.a: Peer Support Groups are student-led, non-clinical peer support. They are not group therapy or crisis services. Facilitators listen, support conversation and connect students with resources; they do not provide diagnosis or treatment.

items.q: Who can attend Peer Support Groups?
items.a: Peer Support Groups are for enrolled UW–Madison students, including undergraduate, graduate and professional students. Check the event details and contact us if you have an eligibility or access question.

items.q: Are Peer Support Groups only for students with mental illnesses?
items.a: Peer Support Groups are open to all students, because we believe everyone can benefit from building a supportive community. Even if you’re not seeking support right now, showing up for a fellow Badger—or learning how to offer support with confidence and compassion—helps break the stigma, anxiety, and stress surrounding mental health.

items.q: How many students are usually in a group?
items.a: You can come on your own or with friends. For questions about group size or the format of a visit, contact our student team.

items.q: When and where do Weekly Groups meet?
items.a: Check the current schedule for each group’s date, time and room. Use the directions shown with the group you plan to attend.

items.q: Who can answer a question about privacy?
items.a: Ask a facilitator what to expect before sharing something you’re unsure about. You can also contact our student team with a general question about privacy or the limits of peer support.

items.q: How can I ask about access or accommodations?
items.a: Please email accessibility@badgersupports.org with an accommodation request or an access question.

items.q: What is Badger Supports’ official email?
a: Our primary email is directors@badgersupports.org. Communications may also be sent to hello@badgersupports.org.
Visit Our Team for the contact details each person shares publicly.

items.q: How can I get involved as a leader?
items.a: You can learn more on our Get Involved page! If you have specific questions not covered there, please don’t hesitate to contact us at hello@badgersupports.org.

items.q: What is your relationship with UHS-Prevention?
a: Badger Supports works with University Health Services - Prevention at UW–Madison on training and consultation.
UHS-Prevention providers review training materials and offer feedback to our student team.

Badger Supports is an independent student organization. Student leaders are responsible for our programs and organizational decisions. We do not represent or speak on behalf of UHS-Prevention unless explicitly stated.

items.q: Are you affiliated with The Support Network?
items.a: No. Badger Supports has no affiliation with any national organization.

blocks.title: Seeing a question not answered?
blocks.body: Reach out at hello@badgersupports.org. On Wisconsin!
